checkpoints.description: [1/4] Pre-register ADR-017 and add failing tests for the hydrogen 2p vortex identification

impact_assessment.why: The first excited state node is singular in 1D. The hydrogen 2p_(m=+-1) state has an angular node at the origin, which is a quantized vortex with circulation h/m_e, not a radial node. Identifying it connects the node problem to the earlier vortex work.
impact_assessment.benefits: A positive fluid-mechanics identification of a real quantum state: circulation, angular momentum and most-probable radius from the exact 2p density.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 26, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; numerical: the azimuthal velocity diverges at theta=0, so the loop is evaluated away from the poles
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the exact 2p radial function; test normalization, the 4a0 peak, the loop circulation away from the poles, and the angular momentum; state that m=0 has no vortex

checkpoints.description: [3/4] Hydrogen 2p: radial normalization 1, peak 4a0, circulation 6.283185307180, loop circulation matches, azimuthal velocity 0.5, Lz=1; claim 26 NUMERIC (vortex identification)

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-018 and add failing tests for the shallow-water acoustic horizon

impact_assessment.why: The user asks which water properties can link to the quantum-fluid program. Shallow-water waves have an acoustic metric set by depth, gravity and flow; a draining vortex has a horizon where the inward flow equals the wave speed, giving an analogue surface gravity and Hawking temperature.
impact_assessment.benefits: A positive water-mechanics link: water properties (h, g, Q) predict a horizon, surface gravity and analogue temperature, contrasting with the nematic director where no emergent metric was found.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 27, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; physics: the acoustic metric is long-wavelength only and breaks under capillary dispersion
impact_assessment.mitigation: Derive r_H, kappa and T_H analytically; test the horizon condition and metric signature; report lab-scale numbers and state the short-wavelength limitation

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-019 and add failing tests for the capillary validity of the acoustic horizon

impact_assessment.why: Claim 27's lab example uses r_H=1.6 mm. Water's capillary length is about 2.7 mm, so the horizon may be in the capillary-dispersion regime, where the long-wavelength acoustic metric does not apply.
impact_assessment.benefits: A design criterion for a valid analogue horizon: the flow rate must make r_H much larger than the capillary length. It prevents overclaiming the lab temperature and uses water's surface tension and density.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 28 and a caveat on claim 27's example; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; physics: the capillary length depends on temperature through gamma and rho
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use water at 20 C (rho=998 kg/m3, gamma=0.0728 N/m); compute ell_c, the capillary/gravity ratio at r_H, the minimum Q for r_H=10 ell_c, and a valid Q example

checkpoints.description: [3/4] Capillary validity: ell_c=2.726879e-3 m; lab r_H=1.607 mm is capillary-dominated (ratio 2.8798); r_H>=10 ell_c needs Q>=1.697e-2 m3/s; Q=0.05 gives ratio 1.152e-3; claim 28 PROVEN
[4/4] Two-run verification 206/206 accepted (2 new claim-28 checks); project gates 4/4; checklists: passed. Uncommitted pending delivery.

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-020 and add failing tests for the dispersive shallow-water horizon

impact_assessment.why: Claim 27 uses the long-wavelength sound speed. The full shallow-water dispersion includes capillary and finite-depth terms, so the horizon depends on wave frequency; the metric is valid only below the capillary frequency.
impact_assessment.benefits: A quantitative frequency-validity condition for the water horizon, complementing the spatial capillary condition of claim 28.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 29, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; numerical: the root equation k c_g + omega_f = omega and the tanh(kh) dispersion
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the exact dispersion (gk+gamma k^3/rho)tanh(kh); test the k->0 limit, the omega_c frequency, and the horizon ratio at low and high frequency

checkpoints.description: [3/4] Dispersive horizon: omega_c=84.824 rad/s; ratios 1.000013 at 0.1, 1.151520 at 10, 5.192407 at 100 rad/s; long-wavelength metric valid below ~1 rad/s; claim 29 PROVEN
[4/4] Two-run verification 208/208 accepted (2 new claim-29 checks); project gates 4/4; checklists: passed. Uncommitted pending delivery.

[1/4] Pre-register ADR-021 and add failing tests for radial rays at the acoustic horizon

impact_assessment.why: The horizon metric is established, but its causal structure has not been checked: radial rays should change direction at r_H and peel away with the surface gravity rate. This tests the analogue horizon beyond the metric components.
impact_assessment.benefits: A positive causal-structure result: the horizon is a separatrix, the peeling rate equals c^2/r_H, and the ray times match the analytic solution.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: new claim 30, no existing claim changes; dependency: numpy only; concurrency: none; state: one result file; numerical: the ray speed vanishes at r_H, so the integration must stop before r_H
impact_assessment.mitigation: Use the valid Q=0.05, h=0.1 regime; derive the analytic ray time; compare RK4 to it; test the sign of the speed on both sides and the peeling rate

checkpoints.description: [3/4] Radial rays: outgoing speed signs -0.110/+0.090 across r_H; ray times match analytic to 2e-6; peeling rate 12.209936 equals surface gravity; claim 30 PROVEN
